column1: # p286 — THE BASIS CHANGED THIS PASS, AND THAT IS WHY THESE NUMBERS MOVED.
# p284 built this ratchet over ONE population: every ladder under compose/code/.  p286
# measured that population and found it counts HISTORY, not EXPOSURE -- 100 of the 117
# `copying` ladders belong to one-off scripts that have already run, 5 carry SUPERSEDED or
# negative-control in their own filename, and only 12 are invoked by `make hooks`.
# 🔴 So a CEILING over the ALL population is the p252 defect again: adding any instrument
# that carries an ungraded ladder turns the gate red while moving risk by zero, which is
# precisely what trained eight passes to bump a number.  Ceilings therefore bind ONLY the
# STANDING population (prefix `STANDING:`), which is the one that can still produce a false
# absence.  Floors stay on the ALL population, where growth is always safe and only a real
# un-closing can breach them.
# Re-derived on p286's basis: case-insensitive extraction from shell `for` lists and exact
# regex alternations, COMMENT-ONLY for prose-only vocabulary, method-attribute exclusion.
# p288 — `IMPORTED-LADDER` is new this pass: a file whose only literal is a status value and
# whose real ladder is READ from an already-CASE-CLOSED module (p284's generator finding, third
# instance).  Re-derived over the whole corpus, it reclassifies EXACTLY ONE row — p288's own
# `probe.sh` — so `STANDING:SINGLE-SPELLING` returns to 17 and no other bound moves.  The floor
# is MIN 1 so a later pass cannot quietly delete the arm and send that row back to a spurious
# `SINGLE-SPELLING`.
# p371 — `STANDING:SINGLE-SPELLING` 17 -> 18, and the reason, because this file's own
# header says a ratchet that cannot carry the reason for its numbers is useless and that
# bumping a number is what eight passes were trained to do.
# WHAT WAS ADDED: `compose/code/p371-backlog-grade/build_backlog.py`, which derives
# `Gap 477`'s backlog from the shelves and stands in `make hooks` as
# `gate-backlog-denominator`.  Its only path-family literal is the token `readme` inside
# `NOT_AN_OWNER` — GitHub's reserved first-path-segments, which the address-shape
# predicate rejects.  The instrument NEVER probes a tree and never decides that a file is
# absent, which is this audit's own scope sentence for when a ladder is a finding:
# "a ladder is only a finding when the instrument uses it to decide that a file is ABSENT."
# TWO CHEAPER OPTIONS WERE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, recorded so the next pass does not
# re-derive them:
#   1. Put a `.lower()` beside the token to earn `FOLD-ON-PATH`.  🔴 Refused: the
#      membership test IS folded, but not within this audit's two-line window, and moving
#      a fold next to vocabulary to flip a grade is exactly the overclaim `_near`'s
#      docstring was written to stop.
#   2. Delete the `readme` token.  🔴 Refused: measured 0 occurrences of
#      `github.com/readme/` in this corpus today, but the ReadME Project publishes
#      `/readme/stories/<name>`, which this base's slug regex WOULD harvest as
#      `readme/stories`.  A guard that currently fires on nothing is still a guard.
# 🟢 What WAS done instead: the instrument now IMPORTS `p235`'s committed `SHELVES` list
# rather than restating it, which removed the file's second readme-family spelling
# (`README.md`) and took the row from `STEM-ONLY` to `SINGLE-SPELLING` — a real
# improvement, and the reason `STANDING:STEM-ONLY` stays at 3.
verdict
